prompts.L1:
Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

Provided are a vaned diffuser and a blower, fluid machine, or electric blower provided with the same, which can achieve both low noise and high efficiency by suppressing mixing loss of standing waves occurring in overlapping sections formed by diffuser vanes, and the main flow in the overlapping sections. The vaned diffuser includes a partition plate, a plurality of vanes provided on one surface side of the partition plate, and a plurality of overlapping sections formed to be sandwiched between the partition plate and adjacent vanes among the plurality of vanes. The partition plate has two holes in a direction orthogonal to each of the overlapping sections, and is provided with a flow path that connects a hole on the inner side in the radial direction among the two holes with a hole on the outer side in the radial direction among the two holes in the adjacent overlapping section.

Provided are a vaned diffuser and a blower, fluid machine, or electric blower equipped with the same, capable of achieving both low noise and high efficiency by suppressing mixing loss between standing waves generated in overlapping sections formed by diffuser vanes and the main flow within the overlapping sections.

The vaned diffuser includes a partition plate, a plurality of vanes provided on one surface side of the partition plate, and a plurality of overlapping sections formed between the partition plate and adjacent vanes among the plurality of vanes. The partition plate has two holes arranged in a direction orthogonal to each overlapping section, and is provided with a flow path that connects, among the two holes, the hole located on the radially inner side with the hole located on the radially outer side in an adjacent overlapping section.
outputs.L2:
A vaned diffuser is described, along with a blower, fluid machine, or electric blower equipped with it. These devices are capable of providing both reduced noise and improved efficiency by limiting the mixing loss between standing waves generated in overlapping regions formed by the diffuser vanes and the primary flow passing through those regions.  

The vaned diffuser includes a partition plate, multiple vanes arranged on one surface of the partition plate, and multiple overlapping regions positioned between the partition plate and neighboring vanes among the plurality of vanes. The partition plate is formed with two openings in a direction perpendicular to each overlapping region. It also includes a flow passage that links the radially inner opening of the two openings to the radially outer opening of the two openings in an adjacent overlapping region.
outputs.L3:
The vaned diffuser is designed to provide both low noise performance and high operating efficiency. Its configuration reduces aerodynamic losses while also suppressing noise generated by pressure fluctuations and standing waves within the diffuser.

In this diffuser, mixing loss between standing waves and the main flow is reduced in the overlapping sections formed by the diffuser vanes. These overlapping sections are located between adjacent vanes, where the flow passages partially overlap in the circumferential direction. By controlling the interaction between the standing wave components and the primary flow, the diffuser can maintain smooth flow behavior and improve overall efficiency.

The diffuser includes a partition plate and a plurality of vanes arranged on one side of the partition plate. Adjacent vanes define overlapping sections that influence the pressure and flow distribution within the diffuser. The partition plate is provided with two holes corresponding to each overlapping section, and these holes are oriented substantially orthogonally to the associated overlapping section.

A flow path is formed to connect the radially inner hole of one overlapping section to the radially outer hole of an adjacent overlapping section. Through this connection, pressure fluctuations can be balanced between neighboring overlapping regions. As a result, the diffuser suppresses the formation and amplification of standing waves, reduces noise, and minimizes mixing losses in the main flow. This structure enables the vaned diffuser to achieve improved acoustic performance without sacrificing aerodynamic efficiency.
outputs.L4:
A vaned diffuser for blowers, compressors, pumps, and other fluid or electric machines is designed to reduce aerodynamic noise while improving operating efficiency. In conventional diffusers, pressure fluctuations can form standing waves in the flow passage. When these standing waves interact with the main flow, especially in regions where diffuser passages overlap or communicate with one another, mixing losses occur. These losses not only reduce the efficiency of the machine but also generate or amplify noise.

The proposed diffuser includes a partition plate and a plurality of vanes arranged to form diffuser flow passages. In the diffuser, certain sections of the passages overlap with adjacent sections, and holes or connecting flow paths are provided so that pressure waves and fluid communication between the passages can be controlled. By appropriately arranging the partition plate, vanes, overlapping portions, and connecting holes or paths, the diffuser alters the behavior of standing waves generated inside the flow passages.

This configuration suppresses the undesirable mixing between the standing-wave components and the main flow passing through the diffuser. As a result, pressure pulsations are reduced, and noise caused by resonance or wave interference is lowered. At the same time, because the main flow is disturbed less and energy loss due to mixing is minimized, the diffuser can recover pressure more effectively.

Accordingly, the vaned diffuser achieves both noise reduction and improved efficiency. It is particularly useful in machines where compact size, high performance, and low acoustic emission are required, such as blowers, fans, compressors, and electric fluid machinery.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent-style abstract for an invention involving a vaned diffuser with a partition plate, diffuser vanes, overlapping sections, and connecting flow paths that reduce standing-wave mixing loss to improve blower efficiency and noise performance.
counterfactuals.output: A vaned diffuser for a blower includes a diffuser passage defined at least in part by a partition plate and a plurality of diffuser vanes arranged circumferentially in the diffuser passage. Adjacent diffuser vanes define diffuser channels through which discharge flow from an impeller is guided. At least one diffuser vane includes an overlapping section positioned to overlap, in a circumferential direction, with a corresponding portion of an adjacent diffuser vane, thereby forming a region in which pressure fluctuations associated with standing waves may occur. The partition plate is provided with one or more connecting flow paths that fluidly connect adjacent diffuser channels at or near the overlapping sections. The connecting flow paths permit pressure equalization and controlled communication of flow between the adjacent channels, thereby suppressing standing-wave formation and reducing mixing loss caused by interaction of unsteady flow components. By reducing standing-wave mixing loss in the diffuser, blower efficiency is improved and aerodynamic noise is reduced.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a technical description of a vaned diffuser and an electric blower equipped with it, emphasizing how the structure suppresses mixing loss of standing waves in overlapping vane sections while maintaining high efficiency and low noise.
counterfactuals.output:
A vaned diffuser is arranged at the discharge side of a centrifugal impeller of an electric blower and converts the dynamic pressure of air discharged from the impeller into static pressure with high efficiency. The diffuser includes a diffuser base portion defining an annular flow passage and a plurality of diffuser vanes disposed circumferentially on the base portion. Each diffuser vane extends generally from an inner peripheral side toward an outer peripheral side of the diffuser and forms a diffuser passage between adjacent vanes.

In the vaned diffuser, at least part of each diffuser vane is arranged so that, in the circumferential direction, an upstream-side portion of one vane overlaps with a downstream-side portion of an adjacent vane. These portions form overlapping vane sections in which adjacent diffuser passages are partially shielded from one another. The overlapping structure guides the high-speed flow discharged from the impeller smoothly into each diffuser passage and suppresses abrupt expansion and separation.

The diffuser is configured so that standing waves generated in the overlapping vane sections are not directly mixed with one another at high intensity. In particular, the vane shape, pitch, inlet angle, outlet angle, passage width, and overlapping length are selected so that pressure fluctuation components generated between adjacent vanes are attenuated or phase-dispersed before merging with the main flow. As a result, the diffuser suppresses mixing loss that would otherwise occur when standing waves formed in neighboring overlapping sections interfere and combine in the flow passage.

More specifically, the overlapping vane sections function as acoustic and aerodynamic control regions. They divide the flow discharged from the impeller into a plurality of guided streams while reducing circumferential pressure pulsation. Since the standing wave energy is confined and weakened within each passage, the pressure waves do not produce strong mutual interference at the downstream merging region. This reduces turbulent mixing, secondary flow generation, and pressure loss. The diffuser therefore maintains a high pressure recovery coefficient while lowering aerodynamic noise.

An electric blower equipped with this vaned diffuser includes an electric motor, a rotating shaft driven by the motor, a centrifugal impeller fixed to the rotating shaft, and the vaned diffuser disposed radially outward of the impeller. Air drawn into the blower through an inlet is accelerated by the impeller and discharged radially outward. The discharged air then enters the diffuser passages formed between the vanes, where velocity energy is efficiently converted into pressure energy.

Because the diffuser suppresses mixing loss of standing waves in the overlapping vane sections, the blower can operate with reduced pressure fluctuation and reduced tonal noise. At the same time, the diffuser passages maintain stable flow guidance and prevent deterioration of pressure recovery. The electric blower therefore achieves high efficiency, low noise, and stable aerodynamic performance even at high rotational speeds.

The structure is particularly effective in compact high-speed electric blowers, where the distance between the impeller outlet and the diffuser inlet is small and pressure pulsations from blade-passing frequency components tend to be strong. By controlling the overlapping vane geometry and the propagation of standing waves within the diffuser passages, the blower reduces acoustic resonance and aerodynamic loss without requiring a large casing or additional silencing components.
counterfactuals.label: cf_3

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate an English patent abstract for a centrifugal blower diffuser comprising a partition plate, multiple vanes, overlapping sections between adjacent vanes, paired holes in the partition plate, and radial inter-section flow paths connecting the holes.

The partition plate is provided with pairs of holes located in association with the overlapping sections, and radial inter-section flow paths are formed to connect the holes of each pair. The radial inter-section flow paths allow fluid communication between regions divided by the overlapping sections of adjacent vanes, thereby suppressing flow separation and pressure loss while improving diffuser efficiency and blower performance.

counterfactuals.prompt: Create a concise invention summary for a fluid machine component: a vaned diffuser whose partition plate includes two holes for each overlap region and a passage connecting an inner-side hole to an outer-side hole in a neighboring overlap region, thereby reducing noise and improving efficiency.
counterfactuals.output: A vaned diffuser for a fluid machine includes a partition plate defining diffuser flow passages between adjacent vanes. In each region where neighboring vane passages overlap, the partition plate is provided with two pressure-communication holes. A connecting passage links an inner-side hole in one overlap region with an outer-side hole in an adjacent overlap region. This arrangement redistributes pressure fluctuations between neighboring passages, suppressing flow pulsation and resonance. As a result, diffuser noise is reduced while pressure recovery and overall machine efficiency are improved.
